week.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.
week.readme: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. They stream tokens, call tools mid-response, update shared state, pause for a human, and spawn subagents, and every framework does it differently. AG-UI replaces that custom wiring with one bi-directional event stream: the agent emits typed events, and any client can render them, no matter which framework built the agent.

Paste a YouTube, Twitch or Kick link (or upload a file) and PeakCut finds the moments worth clipping, cuts them to 9:16, adds word-by-word captions and a hook, and can post them to your connected accounts. new.description: Agent skill for hill-climbing local LLM serving speed (decode, speculative decoding, prefill, KV, startup, TTFT) on any hardware and quantization
new.readme: An agent skill for hill-climbing the speed of a local LLM server on any hardware and any quantization. It covers: single-user and concurrent decode startup time and time to first token It works under a memory cap, and every result has to survive a full-context stability check. It encodes how we actually got these speedups. It is not a list of flags. The workflow: Compute the theoretical ceiling. Measure against interleaved controls. Log every result, including the failures. Gate on long-context retrieval.

new.description: Allo is your friendly neighborhood typeface, free and open source
new.readme: Allo is your friendly neighborhood typeface. It’s variable in weight and roundness, with proportions and curves designed to feel warm without being too cute and clear without being too cold. It’s a perfect companion out of the box, and three variable axes and plenty of alternates let you tune its personality to exactly what you need. Allo is optimized for screens and interfaces, with an optical size that adjusts automatically between text and display.

new.description: PyBot: a chatbot written in pure Python by a swarm of agents. No weights, no training, just rules.
new.readme: LLMs drive today’s chatbots and agents, but chatbots long predate them. Sixty years ago, ELIZA held conversations by matching patterns in what the user typed and answering with predefined templates. It could seem insightful, but its repertoire was narrow, and expanding it meant writing more rules by hand. How far could a rule-based chatbot go if a swarm of agents did that work instead?

new.description: Sculpting, animation and simulation toolkit for pixel-art Gaussian splats
new.readme: A JavaScript toolkit for sculpting signed-distance solids, baking them into pixel-art Gaussian splats, and making them move, react, break, grow and remember what happened to them. Use it from Node, drive it through the ink-studio command, or embed the source bundle in an Inkwell or browser application. The package includes geometry, materials, lighting, animation, character controls, particles, physics, procedural generation, and retained authoring.

new.description: Windows shell replacement in Rust: taskbar, file manager, NTFS search, task manager, disk cleaner. One installer exe.
new.readme: A Windows shell written in Rust: faster and lighter than the stock one. Small native programs (no .NET, no Electron) that replace parts of Windows: the taskbar, File Explorer, file search, Task Manager, plus a disk cleaner, a disk map and a photo viewer. One installer puts them in, one button takes them all out. Download WinRust.exe from the latest release (Windows 10/11, x64). Tick the components you want and press the install button. On a fresh install, rust-explorer is unchecked.

new.description: The open-source Dynamic Island for React, installed with shadcn.
new.readme: A Dynamic Island-style component for any React app, installed with shadcn. Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions. new.description: A 4.5M-parameter two-voice English text-to-speech model, trained from scratch
new.readme: tiny-voca is a small English text-to-speech model. It has two voices, 4.5M parameters, and runs on a CPU or in the browser. Small: 4,537,291 parameters, 18 MB, waveform generator included. Fast: about 70x real time on four CPU threads. Two voices: F2 (female) and M2 (male), American English, 24 kHz. Runs anywhere: PyTorch, ONNX Runtime, and ONNX Runtime Web. Open: code, weights, training recipe and dataset. Trained from scratch. Long text is fine. It is read one sentence at a time and the audio is joined.

PEAR is the training infrastructure behind Training Reasoning Models in Simulation to Natively Use Real Robots, where an open 27B reasoning model learns to use real robots entirely in simulation, with zero demonstrations.

new.readme: Yet another browser. A small, quiet browser for the Mac, with an app for iPhone. Yab is a browser with nothing in the way: a row of tabs, across the top or down the left, and the page. One field takes addresses and searches. Pages run on WebKit, the engine inside every Mac, or, on Apple silicon, on Chromium, per tab or per site. Agents from the AI providers you already pay for can work in tabs of their own, and never see a private tab. One field. Type an address and you go there; type words and you search.

new.description: Heterogeneous Resource Routing and Orchestration
new.readme: Heterogeneous Resource Routing and Orchestration Coordinate tools, models, skills, and agents through executable plans. ExecOrchestra is a heterogeneous resource orchestration framework for complex tasks. It combines tools, models, skills, and agents into executable workflows, allocating generative processing and direct execution as needed. Tools handle explicitly specified operations, while models and agents contribute where generation, judgment, or interaction is required.

new.description: Haru: a low-latency, multilingual, full-duplex spoken dialogue model
new.readme: Haru is a low-latency and multilingual full-duplex spoken dialogue model: it listens and speaks at the same time, the way people do on a phone call. This repository contains the inference code for Haru-4B, a pretrained base model, with three implementations and a web demo. Native full-duplex at 7.5 Hz. Every 133 ms the model takes one frame of the user's audio and produces one frame of its own audio and text.

OpenOrange runs your existing Cloudflare Workers project on AWS, Google Cloud, Azure or your own servers, with no changes to your code. items.title: Document teams can route hard table pages to a second reader using confidence scores
items.connection: Textract Insights gives each extracted value a confidence score and page grounding, and ParseBench-2 names Gemini 4 Neon at low thinking as the top recent model on tables and visual layout, so low-confidence table values can be re-read by the best table parser and compared.
items.context: most extraction errors cluster on complex tables, and human review is the main cost in document pipelines
chain: Textract Insights now attaches a confidence score and a source page to every field it extracts, with no model training.
A router sends only low-confidence values, plus their grounded page, to Gemini 4 Neon at low thinking, which ParseBench-2 ranks first on tables.
Values where both readers agree skip human review, and disagreements go to a reviewer with the exact page attached.
Reviewer time shifts from checking every field to checking flagged ones, so insurers and lenders can take on more document volume per analyst.
items.who: Insurance, lending and accounting operations teams benefit; they or the consultancies building their intake pipelines would pay.
items.versus: Plain single-pass extraction forces either full human review or blind trust, while a confidence-triggered second reader focuses people only where the machines disagree.
items.smallest_test: Run 200 past documents with known correct values through Textract Insights, re-read low-confidence values with Gemini 4 Neon, and count it a success if agreement-only auto-acceptance has under 1% error while sending fewer than 30% of fields to review.
items.disconfirm: Textract confidence scores do not separate right from wrong values, or the two readers agree on the same wrong value on table pages.
